summary: Unexpected slot exhaustion during predictive-autoscale window causing degraded throughput
description:
Issue summary:
During the 09:00-10:00 UTC predictive-autoscale window on 2026-03-12, Nimbus Analytics reported a sustained p95/p99 throughput drop (30-60%) on their reserved pool. The pool reported full GPU slot allocation and started returning 429 throttles and occasional 503s for batched routes.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency p95 increased from ~90ms to ~320ms and p99 from ~420ms to ~1.2s for batched text-generation endpoints.
- Several short streaming requests were failing with streaming disconnects and batch cancellations.
- Billing not affected directly but SLA risk due to degraded throughput.

Environment:
- Dedicated reserved pool (customer: Nimbus Analytics) in prod us-east-1.
- Autoscaler configured in predictive mode (lookback 6h, forecast horizon 1h).
- Pool had pinned model redwood-7b-v1 and fallback llm-open-13b-q4.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Synthetic traffic replay using customer's traffic trace (replay started at 09:00 UTC with same mix of long streaming + many small inference bursts).
2) Observe autoscaler behavior: predictive scale-up initiated ~08:55 UTC, scheduled new slots to be ready at 09:05 UTC.
3) At 09:07 UTC backlog of small short-lived streams increased queueing and slot allocation reached 100%.
4) p95/p99 throughput dropped and some batched inflight requests were cancelled.

Observed logs / traces:
- Grafana dashboard (reserved-pool/nimbus) showed the slot-allocation curve hitting 100% at 09:07 UTC and stayed within 98-100% until 09:40.
- Scheduler logs: "slot_alloc: fail reserve (no_free_slot)" repeated across many hosts.
- Autoscaler logs: predictive job executed and marked new nodes as available, but several allocations failed with "affinity_mismatch" in scheduler.
- Serving runtime logs: repeated "batcher: cancel_batch_inflight: victimous_short_streams" and KV-cache reports show high prefix-cache-built entries.

Notes: customer reported this is first time predictive mode was used at this scale with a mix of many short streams and a handful of long-context generation sessions.
comments: 2026-03-12 09:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Acknowledged. Collected initial logs and asked SRE to pull scheduler and autoscaler traces. SLA flagged and priority set to P1.

2026-03-12 10:02 - SRE (Diego Martinez): Initial hypothesis: slot exhaustion caused by many short-lived streams fragmenting slot capacity and predictive autoscale placing nodes with incompatible affinity. Pulling host-level GPU logs and kernel module messages.

2026-03-12 12:14 - Customer (Nimbus SRE - Rahul Patel): We confirmed traffic spike originates from a localized workflow with thousands of 50-200ms calls every minute; long-run sessions continued concurrently. We can throttle that workflow if needed for troubleshooting.

2026-03-12 15:05 - Eng (Maya Singh): Replayed customer's trace in staging. Reproduction succeeded: short-stream fanout saturates slots and causes the batcher to cancel inflight batches. Observed high KV-cache growth and increased NVLink IO wait on 3 hosts.

2026-03-12 18:30 - Support (Ava Chen): Temporary mitigations applied: 1) Enabled per-tenant short-stream isolation policy (route to separate slot pool) for Nimbus; 2) Increased autoscaler affinity relaxation window. Monitoring impact.
2026-03-13 09:00 - SRE (Diego Martinez): After mitigation, p95 returned to 110-130ms, p99 to ~240ms. Will keep ticket open to track permanent changes and postmortem.
2026-03-13 12:20 - Customer (Rahul Patel): Confirmed improved performance. Asked for guidance to avoid recurrence and whether predictive mode should be used going forward.
investigation_notes:
Findings:
- Root cause appears to be a combination of short-stream fanout and allocation affinity. Short streams create many small batches that fragment slot occupancy (slot-churn), preventing efficient high-throughput batching.
- Predictive autoscaler placed additional nodes, but scheduler reported "affinity_mismatch" for several allocations: the autoscaler offered nodes with constraints (gpu-type:gpuA, zone:a) while existing tenant affinity expected (gpu-type:gpuB or same host family) causing allocations to fail and leaving slots unavailable.
- KV-cache growth: small streams had a high diversity of prefixes; KV-cache eviction wasn't keeping up and memory pressure led to occasional host-level eviction cycles, correlating with small latency spikes.
- NVLink IO wait and GPU kernel queueing observed on 3 hosts; these hosts were running a mix of long-context sessions and many short batches.
- No hardware failures found; kernel messages show resource pressure but not OOMs.

Hypotheses tested:
1) Predictive scale-up nodes with strict affinity caused allocation failures -> validated in staging trace replay.
2) Short-stream isolation reduces slot-churn and should recover throughput -> validated with mitigation in prod for Nimbus.
3) KV-cache tuning (smaller per-tenant cache or different eviction policy) reduces memory pressure -> synthetic tests show lower memory churn but needs longer soak.

Logs / dashboards referenced:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/reserved-pools/nimbus?from=2026-03-12T08:30:00Z&to=2026-03-12T10:00:00Z
- Scheduler trace: https://kibana.redwood.com/app/discover#/doc/trace-id/trace-ff9a3c
- Autoscaler job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/actions/runs/72513
resolution_notes:
Temporary mitigation (2026-03-12):
1) Activated per-tenant short-stream isolation: moved high-fanout short streams for Nimbus into a separate slot pool (isolated small-stream pool) to prevent fragmentation of large-model slots.
2) Relaxed strict autoscaler affinity rules for predictive mode to allow heterogeneous node matches while preserving cost tags.
3) Applied KV-cache eviction tuning for tenant to cap per-tenant prefix entries to 25k (reduced memory churn).

Result: throughput returned to acceptable levels within ~3 hours post-mitigation. Customer confirmed improved p95/p99 metrics and reduced cancelled batches.

Permanent next steps (action items):
- ENG-1729: Update predictive autoscaler to surface affinity mismatch counts and automatically relax affinity when allocation failures exceed threshold. (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cluster-autoscaler/pull/498)
- ENG-1730: Add automatic short-stream isolation heuristic in serving runtime to detect high fanout tenants and route them to separate small-stream pools.
- OPS-881: Run a 72h soak in staging with customer's traffic trace to validate KV-cache eviction changes and measure impact on NVLink IO wait.
- Follow-up with Nimbus: provide best-practice configuration doc for mixed long/short workloads and recommendation to tune client-side batching where possible.

Ticket status: probing for permanent changes; leave open until ENG-1729 and ENG-1730 are implemented and soak completes.
